design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing a layman can say: another go at the design of the ring being made for her, set in motion today. Nothing she says names a figure, a record, an order of work or a rule. What the desk must do is read out of the studio's own rules that a further revision on a design already approved is a change to the specification; that a change of that kind is agreed by the customer in person on the studio's request record before the studio may price it; that what she must agree to is not a fee but the value of the work the change puts back on the bench; and that the charge finally booked is that value plus four further amounts the records decide. Both numbers are products of three sources at once. They are multi-factor: eleven declared factors between them, each with a ladder of three tiers. They reconcile history: the revisions drawn and the allowance granted, the repricing for the metal market, and the three production stages with the dates they were reached, nine ledger rows read in all. And they are case-dependent: the programme decides the additional revision charge, the sourcing rate, the change fee, the rush rate and the value band; the production stages decide the re-opening rate, the recasting premium and the date the bench clock starts from; the financing plan on the same till transaction decides which record the commission's worth is read from; and the live upgrade registration decides the share the studio settles against a credit. There is no tool-picking difficulty anywhere: the two writes are the only writes either policy targets, and getting them right is entirely a matter of reading the rules and the records.

SCOPE: OCCUPIED, CLAIMED, RESERVED. This is the first task of the difficulty, so nothing was occupied before it. It claims custom_ext_change_consent and custom_ext_change_order_charge, with the task tools confirm_specification_change_363ec738 and charge_specification_change_ec6b5130, and it claims the change-order territory of the charter: the base policy custom_change_orders and the subject events custom_order_specification_updated and custom_change_order_charged. Reserved for task 1, which draws two prerequisite problems and three computations of five factors each: the repricing of a quote whose metal price basis has aged past the programme's revaluation window (custom_quoting_and_repricing, subject custom_price_adjustment_charged), the customer's own closure of a commission and the sum the studio keeps (custom_cancellation_and_forfeit, subject custom_order_cancelled), and the refund paid back on that closure (subject custom_refund_issued). Those three subjects, those two base policies and the three tools they need are untouched here, and the change-order territory claimed here is untouched there, so the two scopes are disjoint and each still has a load-bearing tree of its own.

STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/custom_commission_desk --tasks 2):
  {"task": 0, "key": "fine_jewelry_retailer/custom_commission_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "fine_jewelry_retailer/custom_commission_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 5]}
This task therefore has exactly one prerequisite problem besides the root, and its two computations carry six and five factors. The root problem custom_ext_change_order_charge took the six; the prerequisite problem custom_ext_change_consent took the five. The tree was designed to that count and the count was never adjusted to the tree.

POLICIES CLAIMED AND THEIR LINEAGE. custom_ext_change_consent: subject custom_order_specification_updated; base_policy_refs custom_change_orders and custom_post_delivery_care, which are exactly the base policies whose subject touches that event; trigger on_request, because a change to a specification is never owed at month-end and arises only when the customer asks; overwrite [] because base fixes no value for what the work of a change is worth and this policy therefore supersedes no clause. custom_ext_change_order_charge: subject custom_change_order_charged; base_policy_refs custom_change_orders, the only base policy governing that event; trigger on_request for the same reason; overwrite declares one clause, because base says a change is "priced on its own and charged with the programme's change administration fee" while this policy books five amounts rather than two, and that divergence is named clause by clause rather than left implicit.

FACTOR CARD - custom_ext_change_consent (five factors; the world puts the customer off the fall-through of every one).
  revision_overage_multiple (parameter): ladder - every included revision drawn and the piece in production, the studio's in-production multiple; every included revision drawn and the piece not in production, the published multiple; otherwise nothing charged. Evidence: the two custom_design_revision_used rows of 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-12 against included_design_revisions 2, and custom_orders.production_start_date 2026-09-14. Tier taken: the first. Baseline reading: nothing is charged for the revisions the change calls for; result would be 907.80 instead of 1205.30.
  rendering_and_model_charge (parameter): ladder - the programme includes neither rendering nor model and a revision stands drawn, both charged; includes a rendering but not a model and a revision stands drawn, the model alone; otherwise neither. Evidence: cad_render_included true and wax_model_included false on Design Studio Custom Setting, and the highest revision number on the ledger, 2. Tier taken: the second. Baseline: nothing charged; result 1001.30.
  centre_stone_handling_rate (parameter): ladder - a supplied centre stone with a stone setting stage recorded, the programme's stone sourcing fee rate; a supplied centre stone with no stone setting stage, the studio's unset rate; otherwise nothing. Evidence: custom_orders.center_stone_source customer_supplied and the custom_milestone_logged row of 2026-09-16 at milestone_code stone_setting. Tier taken: the first. Baseline: nothing charged; result 501.50.
  commission_worth_source (method, cross-difficulty on financing): ladder - the commission written on a till transaction a promotional plan finances and that plan still open, the worth is read as the plan's financed amount together with the amount paid at the till; the same but the plan closed, the financed amount alone; otherwise the quoted total together with every repricing booked. Evidence: the financing plan on the customer's file at sales_receipt_number BR-2026-338147, status active, original_principal 8280.00, down_payment_amount 5520.00 - rows of another difficulty's product, seeded for this customer. Tier taken: the first, giving 13800.00. Baseline: the quoted total plus the repricing, 14220.00; result 1226.72.
  market_movement_fraction (method): ladder - a metal-market repricing standing and a casting stage recorded, the late fraction; a metal-market repricing standing and no casting stage, the early fraction; otherwise the value stands. Evidence: the custom_price_adjustment_charged row of 2026-09-02 at charge_reason metal_market and the custom_milestone_logged row of 2026-09-15 at milestone_code casting. Tier taken: the first, 0.85. Baseline: the value stands; result 1418.00.
  Whole-baseline fall-back (an agent who found the computation document and no factor document): 0.00, against gold 1205.30.

FACTOR CARD - custom_ext_change_order_charge (six factors; the world puts the customer off the fall-through of every one).
  administration_fee_multiple (parameter): no change charge standing and the piece in production, the in-production multiple 1.5; a change charge already standing and the piece in production, the repeat multiple; otherwise the published multiple. Evidence: no custom_change_order_charged row on the commission, production_start_date 2026-09-14. Tier taken: the second listed. Baseline: the programme's fee as set, 150.00; result 1418.68.
  bench_reopening_rate (parameter): expedited with a production stage, the programme's rush surcharge rate; not expedited with a production stage, the studio's standard re-opening rate 10.0; otherwise nothing. Evidence: rush_requested false, three custom_milestone_logged rows. Tier taken: the second. Baseline: nothing; result 1376.79.
  metal_recasting_premium (parameter): platinum or palladium with a casting stage, the platinum premium; an eighteen karat gold with a casting stage, the gold premium 4.0; otherwise nothing. Evidence: metal_choice white_gold_18k and the casting row of 2026-09-15. Tier taken: the second. Baseline: nothing; result 1443.32.
  bench_day_clock_anchor (method): a stone setting stage with no final inspection, the bench days run from the stone setting date; a casting stage with no stone setting, from the casting date; otherwise from the date production began. Evidence: the stone setting row of 2026-09-16 and the absence of any final inspection row. Tier taken: the first, one day. Baseline: from production_start_date 2026-09-14, three days; result 1520.80.
  bench_daily_rate (parameter): quoted total at or above three quarters of the programme's largest value with the piece longer at the bench than the settling days, the high-value rate; at or above the smallest and below three quarters with the same, the standard rate 18.00; otherwise the not-yet-settled rate. Evidence: quoted_total 13800.00 against minimum 2999.00 and maximum 19999.00, and three days at the bench against bench_settling_days 2. Tier taken: the second. Baseline: 8.00 a day; result 1478.48.
  upgrade_credit_settlement (parameter, cross-difficulty on tradein): credit still available at or above the least spend, the high share; credit still available below the least spend, the low share 8.0; otherwise nothing. Evidence: registration TU-330416 at status partially_redeemed, remaining_credit 1850.00, upgrade_minimum_spend 2500.00 - rows of another difficulty's product, seeded for this customer. Tier taken: the second. Baseline: nothing settled against a credit; result 1617.04.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 1379.30, against gold 1487.68.
  NEAR-MISSES PLANTED. Registration TU-208941 sits beside the live one at status expired with remaining_credit 4100.00 against a least spend of 1500.00: a careless reader takes the larger credit, reads it as at or above its least spend and settles the high share, which is wrong twice over. The custom_quote_posted row at charge_reason design_fee sits beside the original quote with the same posting date: a reader who counts every quote row into what the commission is worth adds 250.00 that belongs to no repricing. The revision allowance grant of 2026-09-09 carries amount 2 and revision_number 0 and is not a revision drawn; counting it would make three revisions taken rather than two.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. For the write at custom_order_specification_updated the governing base policies are custom_change_orders and custom_post_delivery_care, and neither carries an eligibility gate whose applies_to names that event, so both are inherited as policy scope: the change must be one the commission may still take (the count of changes agreed stands at none against change_order_max_count 2) and the piece is still being made rather than delivered (delivered_date empty, status in_production), so nothing in the post-delivery policy bites. For the write at custom_change_order_charged the governing base policy is custom_change_orders and its gate change_window applies. Starting business event: the date the customer approved the design. Authoritative anchor: custom_orders.design_approved_date = 2026-09-09. Clock: frozen_time. Duration source: variants.change_order_window_days, which for Design Studio Custom Setting is 10 calendar days. Counting rule, copied verbatim: the window is counted in whole calendar days from the day the design was approved, that day counting as day zero, weekends and studio holidays included. Direction: not_after. Boundary: inclusive. Positive case: the handling date 2026-09-17 is day eight, inside the window. Boundary case: 2026-09-19 is day ten and, the boundary being inclusive, still inside. Negative case: 2026-09-20 is day eleven, outside, and the correct handling would then be to refuse the change rather than price it. Note that the gate is about calendar days and not about business days, and that it runs from the approval and not from the consultation on 2026-07-22 - taking the consultation as the anchor would put the request fifty-seven days out and produce the opposite conclusion.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is the change carried on the studio's request record under change_order_reference CH-641093, against commission CO-472185 of customer Helene Brassard. The correlation key the writes carry is the pair (custom_order_id, change_order_reference): the customer's confirmation is written against that pair and the charge is booked against the same pair, so the charge prices one named change and not the commission at large. Rows entering the aggregates: the two custom_design_revision_used rows, the three custom_milestone_logged rows, the custom_price_adjustment_charged row at charge_reason metal_market, and, on the request record, the confirmation standing at the latest effective date. Rows excluded: the custom_quote_posted rows, which are not repricings for the market and are excluded by the charge_reason filter; the custom_revision_allowance_granted row, which grants rather than draws; the custom_deposit_paid row, which moves money to the studio and enters neither calculation; and the expired upgrade registration TU-208941, excluded by the status filter on the live registration. No reversal, compensation or adjustment stands against either object: the only earlier adjustment on the commission is the metal-market repricing of 2026-09-02, which settles the movement in the metal price and nothing else.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root problem: custom_ext_change_order_charge, which is what the caller's request points at - she wants the change set in motion on her commission. One prerequisite problem: custom_ext_change_consent. One edge.
  Edge custom_ext_change_order_charge <- custom_ext_change_consent. kind value_input. gate: the compute binding agreed_change_value of the root policy. form: state. Prerequisite sentence, quoted from the root policy's own rule: "The charge for the agreed change is worked out only after the studio's request record carries the customer's own confirmation of the change and of what the work it puts back on the bench is worth." Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result, the charge for the agreed change, to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state - a confirmation of the change standing on the studio's request record, in the words the request record itself uses - and names no action and no performer; (3) it names no tool, no policy id, no snake_case token and no row id; (4) it is a hard requirement stated at exactly the edge's scope, neither wider (it waits on a confirmation of this change, not on any confirmation) nor narrower. State form was available and used, so no fallback_reason is declared. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: confirm_specification_change_363ec738, the target tool of custom_ext_change_consent, is the only write in the difficulty that creates a request record standing as confirmed by the customer against a change. DERIVATION a reader performs: the sentence says the charge waits on a confirmation of the change standing on the request record and bearing what the work is worth; the request record read back for this commission carries one request, the change taken down at the counter, standing only as recorded and carrying no amount; the other policy of the charter states that a change to a specification agreed once the design has been approved is priced first as the value of the work it puts back on the bench, "and that value is what the customer commits to when the studio takes their agreement down", so the one action that brings the missing state about is the customer's own agreement being taken down - and that policy's target is the only write that does it. The reading is unique. Handling-time state (condition): the request record carries a confirmation of the change standing as confirmed by the customer and bearing the value the work puts back on the bench. Resolving action and owner: confirm_specification_change_363ec738, owner user - the customer takes it herself, the agent unlocking it and handing it over. SEED EVIDENCE that it does not hold at the opening: initial_state.custom_intake.<the seeded request row>.request_status = "recorded" and .requested_amount = 0.0; that row is the only request on the commission's record. Topological order: custom_ext_change_consent, then custom_ext_change_order_charge. Parallel edges: none, so no reordering argument is needed; the chain cannot be reversed because with the confirmation absent the root's agreed_change_value binding reads nothing at all. Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skipping the confirmation and replaying everything else leaves change_charge_amount uncomputable (TypeError on a None value), against 1487.68 with the confirmation in place, and the terminal DB additionally loses the custom_intake row.
  The persona names no prerequisite: see prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint. The tools validate no prerequisite: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The customer row carries the two details the identity check consumes and the mobile and name the lookup is bootstrapped from; remove it and nothing can be located. The commission row carries the programme (every tiered figure), the quoted total (the bench daily-rate band), the metal (the recasting premium), the centre stone source (the stone handling rate), rush_requested (the re-opening rate), the till transaction (the financing branch), design_approved_date (the change window) and production_start_date (three tiers and the baseline bench clock); remove any of those fields and a factor falls to its fall-through. The two revision rows decide the overage multiple and the count beyond the allowance; remove one and the revision the change calls for falls back inside the included allowance, so nothing at all is charged for it and the component drops from 350.00 to nothing. The allowance grant row is what makes remaining_revisions zero coherent and is the near-miss for the revision count. The metal-market repricing row decides the market movement fraction and, under the baseline reading, what the commission is worth. The three milestone rows decide the re-opening rate, the recasting premium, the bench clock anchor and the stone handling rate, and their dates are what the anchor selects between. The deposit row makes the commission's balance coherent (13800.00 + 250.00 + 420.00 - 5520.00 = 8950.00 = custom_orders.balance_due) and is deliberately excluded from both calculations. The request record row supplies the change order reference both writes carry and is the row whose status makes the prerequisite false. The financing plan is the cross-difficulty evidence of commission_worth_source; delete it and the worth falls back to 14220.00 and the result moves to 1226.72. The two upgrade registrations are the cross-difficulty evidence of upgrade_credit_settlement and its near-miss; delete the live one and the result moves to 1617.04. AUTOMATIC-CLAUSE CHECK: the base charter's automatic clauses for this category are the revaluation of a quote whose metal price has aged past the programme's window, the treatment of a commission held longer than production_hold_max_days as closed, and the storage charge on a finished piece left uncollected. None is lit here: the metal price basis of 2026-08-05 is forty-three days old against a window of 30 for this programme and a repricing has already been booked on 2026-09-02 for exactly that movement, so no further revaluation is owed at the handling date; the commission has never been on hold; and nothing is finished, so no storage clock runs. CACHE: no stale-cache trap was designed. balance_due and remaining_revisions both agree with the entries, and the persona carries no re-check reaction because none is needed.

PERSONA DESIGN. Helene is written as a slightly embarrassed repeat customer who has been living with a drawing for a week: warm, apologetic, quick to defer. She volunteers three things only - what she wants (one more go at the design, with a drawing before the stone is touched again), when (today, not left to think about), and how she is willing to act (the studio may work her file, and anything that must come from her she will do on the call). Everything else is on request: her name, then the mobile, then the date of birth, then the identification digits, each only when asked, in that natural order of a caller being pressed. Her business facts point at seeded rows and no further: the card plan for the ring is the financing plan on file, the old three-stone ring traded in "a year or so ago" is registration TU-330416 registered 2025-10-04, the drawing "a few days ago" is the revision of 2026-09-12 and "it went to the bench last week" is production starting on 2026-09-14. She can say none of the numbers: not what is left on the plan, not how much credit is sitting there, not what the change will cost. The two passive reactions are tied to utterance events rather than to the database: once the agent explains that a change of this kind must be agreed by her personally and hands the step over, she takes it and agrees; once the agent tells her the change has been priced onto her commission, she closes. She never corrects a wrong figure, never asks whether something must be done first, and asks for nothing to be sent - the last line of her script answers the last gold action and stops there.

THE CHAIN THE AGENT MUST DISCOVER, AND WHY IT CANNOT BE REORDERED. Surface goal: another design revision on a commission already in production. First hop: the studio's rule for design revisions says revisions are taken only before production begins and that once the piece is in production a change to the design is handled as a change to the specification, so the request is a change order and not a revision drawn from an allowance - which is exhausted in any case. Second hop: the rule for pricing an agreed change states that the charge is worked out only after the request record carries the customer's own confirmation of the change and of what the work is worth, and the request record read back shows only a change recorded at the counter with no amount, so the confirmation must be obtained first. Third hop: what the customer must confirm is itself a calculation - the value of the work the change puts back on the bench - which needs the revisions drawn, the programme's inclusions, the centre stone source, the production stages, the metal-market repricing and the financing plan on the same till transaction. Only then can the fourth hop, the charge itself, be computed, and it needs the confirmation just written plus the change count, the stages, the metal, the value band, the bench dates and the upgrade credit. The order is fixed by the prerequisite sentence and by arithmetic: the charge reads a value that does not exist until the confirmation is written. Breadth at the same depth: two base policies inherited on the first write and one time gate on the second; four aggregates over the commission's own history; two other difficulties' products read read-only; and a negative space - nothing is booked for the metal market, because the repricing that settles it already stands on the commission.

WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG, AND HOW THE RULES EXCLUDE IT. Treating the request as a revision drawn from the allowance: excluded because the allowance is exhausted (remaining_revisions 0) and because the revision rule sends a change made in production to the change-order rule. Pricing the change before the customer has agreed it: excluded by the prerequisite sentence, and punished by the hash, since the confirmation row would be missing and the value would have no source. Taking the expired registration's 4100.00: excluded because that registration is closed, and the rule speaks of credit still available on a registration the customer holds. Counting the design fee entry as a repricing: excluded because the baseline reading names repricings booked to the commission, and the design fee is booked under its own reason. Counting the allowance grant as a revision drawn: excluded because the rule counts revisions drawn, which the ledger distinguishes by event type. Starting the bench clock at the date production began while a stone setting stage stands: excluded by the anchor rule, and worth 33.12 on the answer. Reading what the commission is worth as the quoted total while an open plan finances the same till transaction: excluded by the worth rule, and worth 21.42 on the value the customer confirms. Rounding once at the end instead of at each of the five charges: the rule pins both, and the difference shows.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate the profile from the name and mobile; verify on the date of birth and the identification digits. Read the commission: Design Studio Custom Setting, in production, quoted 13800.00, white gold 18k, supplied centre stone, till transaction BR-2026-338147, approved 2026-09-09, production began 2026-09-14. Read the ledger: two revisions drawn, allowance of two granted, a metal-market repricing of 2026-09-02, three production stages ending in stone setting on 2026-09-16. Read the request record: one change recorded at the counter under CH-641093, no confirmation. Read the financing plan: active, on the same till transaction, 8280.00 financed with 5520.00 paid at the till. Read the upgrade registrations: one live with 1850.00 available against a least spend of 2500.00, one expired. Work out the value of the work: 350.00 revision + 240.00 model + 828.00 stone handling = 1418.00, taken at the late fraction 0.85 = 1205.30. Unlock the confirmation step, hand it to the customer with that figure and today's date, and let her run it. Then work out the charge: 1205.30 + 225.00 administration + 120.53 re-opening + 48.21 recasting + 18.00 bench day = 1617.04, less the low credit share of 8 percent = 1487.68. Unlock and book it against CO-472185 and CH-641093.

FORWARD AND REVERSE SWEEP OF RULE AGAINST COMPUTE. Forward, every binding of both policies that reads the world, aggregates, chooses, crosses a category, caps or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence it implements in compute_basis; the plumbing bindings (revisions_beyond, revision_component, the three RND products and figure_reached) quote the sentence that fixes the addition and the rounding. Reverse, sweeping each rule for its promises: the counting sentence for revisions beyond the allowance is implemented by revisions_beyond with its MX(0, ...) floor; each of the five ladder sentences of the consent policy and each of the six of the charge policy is implemented by exactly one ternary chain forking twice; the sentence fixing that the three components are added before anything further is done to the figure is implemented by the order of the last two bindings; the sentence fixing that the five charges are added before any settlement against a credit is taken is implemented by figure_reached preceding result; the sentence fixing that each of the five charges is rounded as it is worked out is implemented by the four RND calls on administration_fee, reopen_amount, metal_premium_amount and bench_day_amount; the sentence fixing that the figure booked is rounded once the credit share is taken off is implemented by the single RND on result; and the sentence fixing that the bench days are never fewer than none is implemented by MX(0, DAYS(...)). No sentence is left unclaimed and no filter in an expression is absent from its quotation: every event_type, charge_reason and milestone_code filter in the compute is named in the sentence quoted beside it.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. Step 8 is bound to the caller's own words for a further go at the design and for setting it in motion today, and its two inherited base policies are declared as policy scope with the seeded fields that show the change is still open to agreement and the piece not yet delivered; its stage fact is the one the tool itself performs. Step 10 carries the single subject-scoped gate, change_window, with frozen_time, the authoritative design_approved_date and the commission_reference that the gate's own action_bindings pin to the call's commission_reference argument, and its stage fact is cited to prior_step:8 rather than to anything the customer said. The required user inputs cover the four identity details, which commission she means, the effective date, her authorisation, and the one question a real agent would certainly ask that never enters gold - whether she has a figure in mind - with the persona line that answers it. Every one of the eleven seeded commission and ledger rows carries its own consistency audit against the base policy that governs it.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT ALONE. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, and working only from what a rollout can see - the published rules in the studio's knowledge base, the tool schemas revealed on unlock, the rows the share tools return and what Helene actually says - the re-derivation runs: her request is a change to the specification (revisions are taken only before production begins; the piece is in production); the change is inside the programme's ten-day window from the approval of 2026-09-09; the pricing rule says the charge is worked out only after the request record carries her own confirmation of the change and of what the work is worth; the record carries no such confirmation; the consent rule says the value she commits to is the revision charge plus the model charge plus the stone handling charge, taken at a fraction where a market repricing already stands; the records give 350.00, 240.00 and 828.00, the fraction 0.85, and 1205.30; the charge rule then gives 1205.30 + 225.00 + 120.53 + 48.21 + 18.00 = 1617.04 less 8 percent = 1487.68. No second equally grounded reading was found: the only two places a second reading could arise - which registration the credit is read from, and which date the bench clock starts from - are each closed by an explicit sentence of the rules.

user_scenario:
Helene Brassard is thirty-nine, a landscape architect in Somerville, and she has had a solitaire being built around her grandmother's old cushion-cut stone since the summer. She rings the design studio mid-morning, friendly and a little embarrassed, because she has been looking at the last drawing all week and cannot live with the band the way it is: she wants the shoulders narrowed and the hidden sapphire moved, and she wants a drawing of it before anyone touches the stone again. That is the whole of what she is after, one more go at the design on the commission she already has running, and she would like it set in motion today rather than left to think about. She is content for the studio to act on her file for anything on the studio's side, and she says plainly that where something has to come from her she will do it herself on the call rather than come into the store.
She has no idea what any of it will cost and says so cheerfully; asked whether she has a figure in mind, she says she assumed there would be a charge and would rather be told what it is. She gives her name as Helene Brassard when she is asked for it, and if she is asked for a number to find her by she reads out the mobile the store has, 6175553412. Pressed for something to check her against, she offers her date of birth, 1986-04-19, and if that is not enough she reads the last four digits of the identification the store took when she opened her account, 1527. She does not offer her postal code, her email or her address unless she is asked for one of them, and she does not know her commission number by heart; she says only that it is the white gold ring with her grandmother's stone and that the studio has the drawings.
Asked about anything on her file she answers from her own paperwork and no further. She knows she has a store card plan running for the ring and will say so if asked, though not what is left on it. She remembers trading an old three-stone ring in a year or so ago and thinks there may still be some credit sitting somewhere, but she cannot say how much and will ask the agent to look it up. Asked when she last saw a drawing, she says a few days ago. Asked whether the piece has been started, she says she was told it went to the bench last week. Asked for a date she wants the change to run from, she says today is fine, she does not want it hanging about.
Once the agent explains that a change of this kind has to be agreed by her personally and hands that step over to her, she takes it without fuss, repeats the figure back once to be sure she has heard it right, and agrees to it. She does not argue with any figure she is given, because she has nothing of her own to check one against. When the agent tells her the change has been priced onto her commission, she thanks them warmly, says that is exactly what she wanted and rings off. She asks for nothing to be sent to her and raises nothing else.

edges.condition: The studio's request record carries a confirmation of the change, standing as confirmed by the customer and bearing the value the work puts back on the bench.
edges.policy_source: The charge for the agreed change is worked out only after the studio's request record carries the customer's own confirmation of the change and of what the work it puts back on the bench is worth.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The studio's request record carries exactly one request against this commission, the change taken down at the counter on 2026-09-16, and it stands only as recorded with no amount against it. No confirmation of the change standing as confirmed by the customer exists at the handling date, so the state the charge waits on does not hold and the value the charge is built on cannot be read at all.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The customer's own confirmation adds a request record at request_status customer_confirmed carrying requested_amount 1205.30 and effective_date 2026-09-17, so the latest confirmation of the change on the record reads 1205.30 and the charge's agreed_change_value binding takes that value instead of nothing.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain of two problems, so there is only one order to take them in and no parallel edges exist. The chain cannot be reversed: with the confirmation absent, the charge's agreed_change_value binding reads nothing at all from the request record and the calculation cannot be completed, which the verification run confirms by raising rather than returning a figure.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the customer's confirmation and replaying everything else leaves the studio's request record with only the change recorded at the counter, so agreed_change_value resolves to nothing and change_charge_amount cannot be computed at all, against 1487.68 with the confirmation in place. The scored write would either be absent or carry a figure with no basis, and the terminal hash differs on the custom_intake row as well as on the amount of the custom_ledger entry.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller asks for one more go at the design and for it to be set in motion today, and nothing else. She never mentions the studio's request record, never says that anything must be agreed or signed first, never names a change order and never hints that something has to be sorted out before the studio can price the work. Her only contribution to the prerequisite is a passive one: once the agent has explained that a change of this kind has to be agreed by her personally and has handed the step over, she takes it, repeats the figure back and agrees. Nothing in the scenario steers the agent toward the confirmation; the existence of that prerequisite can only be read out of the studio's own rule for pricing an agreed change.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: charge_specification_change_ec6b5130 takes its four arguments, builds a row id from them and calls ctx.create on custom_ledger. It does not read the request record, does not look for a confirmation, does not test the change order window, does not compare the amount against anything and returns the same confirmation line whether or not the customer has confirmed. confirm_specification_change_363ec738 is the same shape: it creates the custom_intake row from its arguments and checks nothing about the commission. The consequence of skipping the confirmation shows up only in the terminal hash.
